LESSON: INTENSIVE SIGN READING DESCRIPTIVE FICTIONAL OR NON-FICTIONAL TEXTS (ABOUT 400 WORDS)

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.1: Intensive Sign Reading Descriptive Fictional or Non-Fictional Texts (about 400 words)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Intensive Sign Reading Descriptive Fictional or Non-Fictional Texts (about 400 words), part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five General.

Key inquiry question: How do you describe things? 2. How can you tell what will happen in a story?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognise signs of vocabulary related to the theme,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Intensive Sign Reading Descriptive Fictional or Non-Fictional Texts (about 400 words) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. value the importance of focus on detail when reading a text. • In groups, learners are guided to watch a demonstration or signed video clip with vocabulary related to communicable diseases. • In pairs, learners are guided to identify, fingerspell and articulate signs of vocabulary related to communicable diseases. • In groups, learners are guided to make connections between events in the text and their experiences. • In groups, learners are guided to retell as they sign the story. • In pairs, learners are guided to use illustrations, the introduction and the title of a text to make predictions. • In groups, learners are guided to describe as they sign the characters, episodes and places in a text. • In groups, learners are guided to scan a text for specific details. • In pairs, learners are guided to answer questions from a text. • In pairs, learners are guided to say as they sign the main ideas from a text. • In pairs, learners are guided to watch a signed video related to the theme and pick specific information. 1. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Intensive Sign Reading Descriptive Fictional or Non-Fictional Texts (about 400 words) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination: Making observations as learners make connections between events in the text and their experiences.

• Digital literacy: Interacting with digital technology as learners watch a signed video related to the theme and pick specific information.

Values:
Responsibility: Hard works as learners answer questions from a text.

Link to other Subjects:

Learners are able to relate the concept of communicable diseases to their learning in Environmental Studies, Science and Technology, Creative

Arts.
